To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the flow rates of the 15 APS units were within 2–5 % of their nominal values, the sizing accuracy was within 10–15 %, the unit-to-unit differences of the particle number concentration were within 5–20 % for particle sizes between 0.9 and 3 µ m, and the differences increased for particle diameters below 0.9 or larger than 3 µ m.

the APS 3321 is a reliable instrument for atmospheric measurements and that the sizing uncertainty of the APS 332, which has been used in the ACTRIS aerosol network for many years, is 10 % for particles larger than 1 µm.
the unit-to-unit differences of the APS 3321 in terms of the number size distribution were within 10 %, for particles between 0.9 and 3 µμm, but were larger than 20 % below 0.9 µm and above 3 µm.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a better understanding of the uncertainties of APS measurements.
the quality assurance of the APS model 3321.
the intercomparison of the particle number concentration and size distribution of 15 aerometric particle size spectrometry units.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the APS model 3321 is an appropriate instrument to measure the particle number size distributions in the coarse mode of the atmospheric aerosol.
the 15 units investigated are comparable in their performance.
the 15 APS 3321 units are suitable for measuring the number concentration and the size distribution of coarse particles (0.5–5 µm) in the atmosphere with a high degree of confidence.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the APS is a robust instrument for atmospheric measurements of coarse mode particles.
the APS model 3321 is a reliable and robust instrument for atmospheric aerosol number size distribution measurements in the size range from 0.9 to 3 μm, if a proper calibration is performed.
a high quality of the APS 3321 is achieved if the flow rate is known and stable and if the sizing accuracy is within 10 %.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a careful quality assurance and intercomparison is essential for atmospheric aerosol networks to ensure comparable results.

the intercomparison of 15 units of one APS model 3321 shows that the instrument is suitable for atmospheric measurements, but the uncertainty in particle sizing and counting efficiency must be taken into account.
a careful quality assurance and quality control is required to obtain reliable data with known uncertainties.
